h1: The 4 Best LG Cordless Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best LG Cordless Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four LG CordZero cordless vacuums compared on listed runtime, form factor and price tier, with a pick for every home.
summary: The LG CordZero Cordless Stick Vacuum with the 120 minute runtime is the best overall pick for larger homes. The original CordZero handheld-capable model suits buyers who want a flexible tool, the older 100 minute stick is the value choice, and the Q3 is the newer option for mixed flooring.
intro: The most common mistake with LG cordless vacuums is buying on the name alone. LG sells several CordZero generations side by side, and the listings look nearly identical while runtime and price tier differ.

We ranked the four LG models in our product pool on the figures each listing publishes: runtime, form factor and price bucket. Brand-only titles need real LG products, so we left out every other maker.

products.name: LG CordZero Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The longest listed runtime of any LG here makes it the easy default.
products.description:
This CordZero stick lists a 120 minute runtime, the longest figure among the four LG models we ranked. It sits in the $200-500 bucket and is sold as a cordless stick.

It ranks above the other stick because of that runtime edge. The 100 minute stick below costs less, so the tradeoff is paying more for the extra 20 minutes.

Buy it if you clean a whole floor or a larger home in one pass. Runtime is a listed figure, and real minutes drop at higher power settings.
products.idealFor: Owners of larger homes who want fewer charging stops.
products.skipIf: Your space is small and a cheaper stick covers it.

products.name: LG CordZero Vacuum
products.verdict: A 100 minute CordZero that also lists a handheld mode.
products.description:
This CordZero lists 100 minutes of runtime and a handheld configuration, in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks second because it trails the top pick by 20 minutes of listed runtime while costing the same tier. What it adds is the handheld use that the listing calls out.

Choose it for stairs, cars and furniture as well as floors. If you only vacuum open floors, the longer runtime above is the better use of the same budget.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want one tool for floors and small jobs.
products.skipIf: You want the longest possible runtime.

products.name: LG CordZero Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The cheapest LG here, with the same 100 minute runtime as the pricier handheld.
products.description:
This older CordZero stick lists 100 minutes of runtime and lands in the $100-200 bucket, a full tier below the top two.

It ranks third because it gives up the 120 minute figure of the leader, but it also saves real money. Against the handheld-capable model above, it matches the runtime and drops the handheld listing.

It suits apartments and first-time LG buyers. Its price tier means it is the safest way into the CordZero range.
pros: Lowest price tier of the LGs
products.idealFor: Apartment owners who want LG on a tighter budget.

products.name: LG Cordzero Q3 Cordless Stick Vacuum Cleaner with Auto Multi-Surface
products.verdict: The Q3 is the newest name, but its listing gives us the least to compare.
products.description:
The Q3 is a cordless stick with an auto multi-surface label, priced in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks last only because its listing publishes no runtime figure. The three models above give a number, and a vacuum you cannot size on paper is a riskier buy.

Pick it if the multi-surface label matches mixed hard floor and rug at home, and check the full listing for runtime before you order.
products.idealFor: Homes that mix hard floor and rugs.
products.skipIf: You need a published runtime before buying.

whatMatters.detail: Runtime is how many minutes the vacuum runs on a full battery. It matters because a short runtime means mid-clean charging stops in bigger homes. Find the minutes in the listing bullets and treat them as the best case, since higher suction modes drain faster.

Some cordless vacuums detach from the pole and become a hand tool. That matters for stairs, upholstery and cars, where a full stick is awkward. Look for a handheld mention in the listing title or specs.

LG keeps older and newer CordZero models on sale together, with similar names. A newer generation can change features, while an older one usually costs less. Compare the model name and the price tier rather than assuming they match.

Homes with both hard floor and rugs benefit from a vacuum that adapts to surfaces. An auto multi-surface label suggests this, but it is a feature name, not a promise. Read the listing description to see what it actually does.

A listing with clear numbers lets you compare models on paper. When a figure like runtime is missing, you are guessing. Prefer models that state their specs, or confirm the missing number before buying.

faq.q: Are all four of these actual LG vacuums?
faq.a: Yes. Each carries the LG CordZero or Cordzero name in its listing, and we dropped other brands from the comparison.

faq.q: Is the 120 minute model worth it over the 100 minute one?
faq.a: Only if your home needs the extra time. The 100 minute stick is in a cheaper bucket and covers an apartment.

faq.q: Why does the Q3 rank last?
faq.a: Its listing gives no runtime figure, so it cannot be compared on paper. It may still suit mixed floors.
It lets the vacuum come off the pole for stairs, cars and furniture. The LG CordZero Vacuum is the one that lists it.

faq.q: How should I read the runtime numbers?
faq.a: Treat them as the best case. Stronger suction settings usually shorten the real minutes.

faq.q: Do the two CordZero sticks differ?
faq.a: They share a name but differ in listed runtime (120 versus 100 minutes) and price tier. Check the model before ordering.

finalTake: For most homes, the LG CordZero Cordless Stick Vacuum with 120 minutes is the best LG you can buy. Apartment owners should take the 100 minute stick and keep the savings. The handheld-capable CordZero fits stair-heavy homes, and the Q3 is worth a look once you confirm its runtime.
